relevance_note: Case report of a girl with Blau syndrome and a NOD2 variant ("she had a de-novo heterozygous mutation in the NOD2 gene (c.1538 T > C, p.M513T)"), plus a supplementary table of 8 Blau syndrome children from the same center and a literature table of Blau patients with vasculitis.
method_note: Read the whole paper (text, Table 1, supplementary Table S); built the JSON with a short Python script in my scratch directory that copies table-row segments directly from the Markdown and asserts every span is found verbatim; the script's table transcription was checked by eye against both tables. People: (1) the case-report girl ('patient'); (2) her two parents, tested by WGS and wild type ('parent of patient', 'parent of patient 2'; sex not stated; no variant rows); (3) the 8 children of supplementary Table S ('Clinical data of 8 children with blau syndrome in our center'), labelled 'Table S #<No>'; (4) the eight single-case rows of literature Table 1, labelled 'Table 1 row <k>' (k counting data rows from the top), with the 'Year,author' cell as source_reference_in_review. Left out: Table 1 row 1 (Rotenstein [8], '2/F') and row 10 (Li [17], '8/NA') because they describe groups of 2 and 8 patients with row-level marks only (group level); Table 1 row 11 ('2022,Our medical center', 1/F, M513T) is this paper's own patient and is used only as context. NOT MERGED BUT VERY LIKELY THE SAME PERSON: Table S #7 (Female, diagnosed 2019, onset 0.83 y, first visit 7.67 y, diagnosis 17.83 y, R/A/U/F/V/HBP/RI, M513T) matches the case patient (rash at 10 months, first visit at 7 years 8 months, diagnosed at 17 in 2019, M513T), but the paper never states that row 7 is the case patient, so both rows are kept; downstream deduplication should consider merging them. Table S: '\*' is defined as 'the patient had this clinical manifestation'; blank cells are undefined and recorded as not reported. Ages in Table S are in years (header 'Age(year)'), converted as P<n>Y with decimals kept; 'First visit' age and 'Initial symptom' have no schema field and were not recorded. RI (renal involvement), LI (liver involvement) and CI (cardiac involvement) were recorded as phenotypic features but not mapped to the narrower checklist items (renal failure, hepatomegaly, pericarditis). Table S gives no gene name in the 'Mutation' column; gene NOD2 is taken from the paper's statement that Blau syndrome is caused by NOD2/CARD15 mutations. Table S #3 has Mutation 'NA', so no variant row. Table S #6 'M513A' recorded as printed. Table 1: '^a' is defined as the patient having the manifestation; blank cells are undefined (not reported); 'NA' is not reported. For Table 1 people whose vascular cell does not name arteritis/vasculitis (rows 2, 4, 5, 6: renal/mesenteric artery stenosis, abdominal aortic aneurysm, 'large-vessel', sinus of Valsalva aneurysm), the vasculitis checklist item is marked observed as 'inferred from group statement' from the table title ('published cases with pediatric Blau syndrome and vasculitis'). Not used: the text's 'Arthritis was the most frequent clinical feature, with a frequency of 100%', which conflicts with blank or NA arthritis cells for Gedalia [11], Mourad [13] and Amin [16] (contradiction within the paper; those cells left not reported). Case patient time-varying findings: CRP/ESR significantly increased in August 2009, within normal ranges in October 2019, ESR increased (25 mm/h) in December 2022; rash at 10 months but absent in August 2009 and December 2022. These are different time points, not contradictions; both observed and excluded feature rows are emitted with the timing in severity_or_detail, and the checklist items (rash, elevated inflammatory markers) are marked observed. Normal echocardiography/ECG and 'No other remarkable findings ... on physical examination' were not used to exclude pericarditis, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. Vital status 'alive' rests on 'A girl, now 20 years old'. Inheritance de novo: the paper states WGS of the family with both parents wild type. Pathogenicity left not reported ('has been reported previously' is not a classification). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not say its own patients were published before (the literature-table people carry their references in source_reference_in_review). cohort_size_as_stated = 8 from the Table S title; n_patients_reported left null (no stated count of NOD2-variant patients).
